title: Google Messages launches major homepage overhaul: integrates Gemini shortcut, restructures pinned and bottom search

content_html:
November 7 news: Google is advancing a major homepage redesign for Google Messages on Android. The update has now entered the testing phase and is gradually rolling out to some beta testers. This redesign covers three core components, aiming to optimize the interface layout and make one-handed operation more convenient.

In terms of visual and interaction layout, the new version prominently elevates pinned chat avatars to the very top of all conversation lists, using the existing background layer to display large contact avatars. Meanwhile, Google has turned the search function into a centered floating action button (FAB) next to the new chat button, which takes on a pill-shaped dynamic scaling effect as the user scrolls the page. In addition, the original Gemini floating action button has been repositioned next to the profile picture in the upper-right corner, consistent with the design guidelines for Workspace apps on desktop and mobile.

This interface restructuring reflects the ongoing evolution of interaction logic in mainstream instant messaging products. As large model capabilities become more deeply integrated into native system apps, streamlining entry points and optimizing the flow for high-frequency functions have become key paths for platforms to increase user stickiness, and they also lay the foundation for the seamless integration of multimodal interactions in the future.
